title: GDD T-107 — Adaptar MECH_02 ¡ESQUIVA! al contrato; completar MECH_03 ¡CORRE!; crear MECH_01 ¡MANTÉN! (§4)
description: Consolidates the three Hito 2 competitive mechanics per GDD §4, on the canonical §10.2 contract (GDD-authority decision 2026-07-07: code adapts to the GDD). (A) MECH_02: adapt the existing EsquivaMicrogame/Esquiva-3D dodge base to the v2 IMicrogame contract, conserving existing tests; normalized [0,1]² arena, deterministic seeded hazards (patterns Rain/Sides/Cross/Homing_soft with 30°/s turn cap guaranteeing escape), one hit eliminates, ranking by survival tick. (B) MECH_03: complete the endless-run per spec — button MASH accelerates (v = vBase + vGain·mashNorm via the §3.3 curve from InputInterpreter), stick-up TAP jumps (never the reverse mapping), identical seeded obstacle tracks in all 4 lanes, obstacle hit = 0.6 s stun (no elimination), rubber-band +8% vBase for last place; the existing RunnerSim (Endless Run demo) is the code base to adapt — fold in the still-pending human camera UAT verdict at the View level. (C) MECH_01 ¡MANTÉN!: new inverted-pendulum balance per §4 — theta'' = (g/L)·sin(theta) + perturbacion(t) − k·input with seeded noise amplitude ramp A(t) = A0 + rampa·t, fail at |theta| > thetaMax (35° default), L/R torque only, victory = last standing or lowest mean |theta|. The Alcocheck demo sim is prior art to mine, not a constraint. All three declare difficultyScaling fields in their v2 definitions. NOTE for orchestrator: large ticket — consider splitting into 3 sub-tickets at execution time; Annex D.5 lists it as one row. Read GDD §4 (MECH_01/02/03), §10.2, §9.1 before coding.
acceptance_criteria: All three mechanics implement the canonical v2 IMicrogame contract as engine-free Core sims with injected SeededRandom and zero-alloc steady Tick

MECH_02: escapability test — an optimal bot survives full duration on every seed in the test set; no overlapping spawns (min separation 0.08); Homing_soft turn rate capped 30 deg/s; existing dodge tests conserved or migrated

MECH_03: same seed produces the identical track in all 4 lanes; a bot at constant 6 Hz mash with perfect jumps finishes unstunned; rubber-band never inverts the result between two players with identical mash over 1000 seeds (statistical test)
MECH_01: with null input every pendulum falls before duration on all test seeds; with simulated perfect correction 100% survive; replay determinism test passes
Each mechanic's v2 definition declares its difficultyScaling params and passes the TASK-030 validator
Ranking edge cases per GDD: simultaneous eliminations share Place; survivors at timeout share 1st (MECH_02); ties handled without fabricated winners
Tests-first (red before impl) for all new/changed rules; fast suite green after, no regression; existing legacy consumers keep compiling

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body: [RE-APPLIED] SCOPE ADDITION from the TASK-035 review (rev-c035, 2026-07-07): the T-108 MicrogameSelector was built as a V2 SUCCESSOR (Barcade.Core.Sequencer.V2) coexisting with the v1 SequencerDirector, because v1 contains a GDD P3-violating re-roll loop (SequencerDirector.cs:117-122 — multiple draws per decision) and in-place extension would have dragged the whole T-107 migration into T-108. That coexistence reading of GDD 9.2 ('código existente, se extiende') is defensible ONLY as a transition state: this ticket (T-107 migration) MUST retire the v1 SequencerDirector (or at minimum remove its re-roll loop and route all consumers through the V2 selector) so the deviation does not become permanent. Verify at review time that no production consumer references v1 after this ticket closes.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body: CARRY-IN from TASK-029 (ratified deferral, 2026-07-07): when reconciling the four pre-GDD legacy ids (aporrea/apunta/timing/recolecta) against the canonical MECH_01..09 set per this ticket's T-107 scope, the un-debounced ButtonState.Pressed edge consumption in AporreaMicrogame (raw per-tick edge counting — bounce inflates mash counts), TimingMicrogame and ApuntaMicrogame-v1 (one-shot latch — bounce can land the single decision early) MUST be resolved as part of each mechanic's fate: a v2-native rewrite gets an owned InputInterpreter (edge detection per GDD §3.2, the Reacciona/Apunta-v2 pattern — note the interpreter's 2-tick debounce-confirm delay is a real behavior change vs raw edges; retune thresholds/tests accordingly); an explicit retirement removes the concern with the code. Do NOT port raw ButtonState.Pressed reads into any surviving mechanic. Origin: TASK-023 review LOW-2; inventory verified in TASK-029's decision record.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body: CARRY-IN from TASK-052 review (rev-t052 LOW-3, 2026-07-07): whichever slice of this ticket wires the V2 selector/definitions into SessionStateMachine (the v1-SequencerDirector retirement condition) must (a) add an integration test pinning MicrogameDefinitionV2.PayoutTable -> SetActiveMicrogame -> CaptureResult -> Coins for a validator-passed definition, and (b) handle the null-vs-empty asymmetry: MicrogameDefinitionV2.PayoutTable defaults to Array.Empty<int>() (MicrogameDefinitionV2.cs:62) while the FSM's §6.1-defaults fallback triggers only on NULL (SessionStateMachine.cs ~630/644) — passing an unvalidated default POCO's empty table causes a round-end throw instead of fallback. Either normalize at the wiring site (empty -> null) or document-and-test the chosen semantics; add the SetActiveMicrogame doc sentence that empty != fallback. The opt-in optional parameter compiles fine when forgotten (fallback masks omission) — the integration test is what catches a silently-unwired payoutTable.

comments.author: dev-t101
comments.body:
PHASE A SPLIT PROPOSAL (read-only, no code). Read GDD §4 MECH_01/02/03, §9.1/9.2/§10.2 + all named prior-art firsthand.

GROUNDING FACTS: (1) EsquivaMicrogame.cs (v1 Core, 4-player one-hit-eliminates FFA) is the MECH_02 sim base — NOT DodgeSim/Esquiva-3D, which GDD §10.4 confirms is a VIEW/style reference only. (2) RunnerSim (Endless Run) is a bigger mismatch than the ticket implies: MECH_03's GDD control scheme is ONLY mash-accelerate + stick-up-tap-jump ('nunca al revés'); RunnerSim currently ALSO has slide + lane-switching + auto-accelerate + per-instance independent RNG — adapting it means stripping lane-switch/slide, swapping auto-accel for the §3.3 mash curve, elimination->0.6s stun, and re-architecting to ONE seed = identical track across all 4 lanes. (3) AlcocheckSim is structurally close to MECH_01 but uses discrete uniform re-roll, not GDD's continuous ramping A(t)=A0+ramp·t; no engine-free noise primitive exists in Core. (4) MicrogameSelector's own doc already says v1 SequencerDirector 'retires under T-107'; the P3-violating re-roll loop is SequencerDirector.cs:117-122; BUT Framework production (SessionController/MicrogameLoopController/HudController/PlayerCornerHud) references v1 today and Sequencer.V2 has ZERO Framework consumers — a full swap = a TASK-055-scale wiring project, not a T-107 side effect. (5) The 4 legacy ids (aporrea/timing/apunta-v1/recolecta) map to NO canonical MECH_01-09; recolecta especially has no home; MicrogameHost.cs registry is the wiring point. (6) MechanicParamSchemas.cs only has MECH_04/05 entries — each new slice adds its own.

PROPOSED 5 SLICES: SLICE 0 = P3 fix (replace SequencerDirector re-roll do-while with filter-then-single-draw; minimal reading of comment-1, NOT the full Framework V2 swap — flag that as a separate follow-up; owns comment-1; XS, no Editor gate, blocks nothing, runs first). SLICE 1 = MECH_02 (adapt EsquivaMicrogame: normalize [0,1]², 4 named seeded patterns, 0.08 min separation, 30°/s Homing_soft cap, Ranked-by-survival-tick result; owns AC1-share/AC2/AC5-own/AC6-MECH_02/AC7-share; M, Core-only, View out). SLICE 2 = MECH_03 (largest delta; owns AC1-share/AC3/AC5-own/AC6-share/AC7-share; L, size hinges on ambiguity #1; sequence last among mechanics; camera UAT is View-level §10.4). SLICE 3 = MECH_01 new (AlcocheckSim as partial prior art + new noise layer; owns AC1-share/AC4/AC5-own/AC6-share/AC7-share; M). SLICE 4 = legacy-id reconciliation (per-id retire-vs-v2-rewrite for aporrea/timing/apunta-v1/recolecta, each a named owner per comment-2; touches MicrogameHost registry + generator Specs + on-disk assets for retirees; M-L; parallelizable; Framework registry touch Unity-gated). AC7 cross-cutting (each slice owns its share).

RECOMMENDATION: TASK-034 becomes an UMBRELLA closed when all 5 slices close (not executed under its own key) — different sizes, an ambiguity-dependency, and two qualitatively different carry-ins deserve separate review attention.

GDD AMBIGUITIES NEEDING HUMAN RULING (surfaced to human via orchestrator): #1 MECH_03 — one fixed lane per player + jump-only (dev reading) vs RunnerSim-style lane-switching? (biggest sizing swing). #2 (tied to #1) MECH_03 keeps duck/slide + high obstacles, or jump the only avoidance? #3 MECH_01 — build engine-free Perlin, or documented seeded-noise substitute [ASSUMED]? #4 MECH_01 — keep AlcocheckSim's damping term as [ASSUMED] deviation (Euler stability) vs GDD-literal no-damping ODE? #5 MECH_02 — the four pattern names have NO geometric definition in the GDD; provide definitions or sign off on the engineering [ASSUMED] (Rain=top-down fall / Sides=L-R entry / Cross=diagonal corner-to-corner / Homing_soft=slow-turn toward nearest player).
